claims.claim: One round has the exact form T(p)=reverse(p_i : i in D) followed by (p_i : i not in D), where D={i>=2 : p_i<p_{i-1}} and both subsequences otherwise retain index order.
claims.evidence: The scan fixes D before any movement. If the marked values in scan order are m_1,...,m_k, successive MoveToFront operations leave them as m_k,...,m_1. Unmarked values never change relative order. The checker independently compared this formula with literal queued MoveToFront execution on every permutation through n=9.
claims.search_method: Direct proof from the marking pseudocode, supplemented by exhaustive comparison on all 409,113 permutations of sizes 1 through 9.

claims.claim: There is an exact reduction of every maximum-element phase to parallel deletion in a word. Once i+1,...,n are fixed, write the active prefix as L i R. Define A(r_1...r_s)=(r_j : 2<=j<=s and r_{j-1}<r_j). The number of further rounds until i is fixed is h(R)=min{t:A^t(R) is empty}.
claims.evidence: The active prefix contains exactly 1,...,i, so i cannot be marked. If R is nonempty, r_1 is marked because r_1<i; for j>=2, r_j is unmarked exactly when r_{j-1}<r_j. Claim 0 therefore leaves precisely A(R), in original order, to the right of i. The fixed larger suffix is untouched, so iteration gives the asserted extinction time, including h(empty)=0. Direct execution and phase totals agreed for every permutation through n=9.
claims.search_method: Invariant proof for the suffix right of the active maximum; exhaustive direct-versus-phase comparison through n=9; literal deletion and monotone-stack extinction were also compared on every permutation word through length 9.

claims.claim: If W(n) is the worst-case number of nontrivial rounds, then W(n)<=n(n-1)/2. Consequently no permutation family requires omega(n^2) rounds.
claims.evidence: Partition an execution into successive phases for active maxima n,n-1,...,2, with length zero when a maximum is already fixed. A nonempty word of length s is mapped by A to at most s-1 entries, hence its extinction time is at most s. The phase for i starts with |R|<=i-1, so it lasts at most i-1 rounds. Summing gives W(n)<=sum_{i=2}^n(i-1)=n(n-1)/2. Dividing by n^2 uniformly bounds every family and rules out omega(n^2). The bound was also checked on every permutation through n=9.
claims.search_method: Rigorous phase-length summation using Claim 1, plus exhaustive finite counterexample search through n=9.

claims.claim: For p_n=(n,1,2,...,n-1) and n>=3, at least n-1+floor((sqrt(8(n-1)+1)-1)/2) rounds are required.
claims.evidence: With B_0 empty and B_{m+1}=(m+1)T(B_m), induction using Claim 0 gives T^t(p_n)=B_t,n,t+1,...,n-1 for 0<=t<=n-1. Thus n fixes after n-1 rounds, leaving B_{n-1},n. The monotone-stack deletion recurrence assigns an entry one plus the maximum label among smaller entries it pops; appending-entry induction proves these are exact deletion rounds. Writing m=q(q+1)/2+r with 0<=r<=q, induction on the B recurrence gives maximum label q, with the degenerate m=1 base handled separately. For m>=2 the initial maximum in B_m and in B_m without that maximum have the same first A-image, so the next maximum requires q additional rounds. Substituting m=n-1 proves the bound. Exact-integer checks validated the stack invariant through m=1000 and complete family executions through n=100.
claims.search_method: Induction on the special-family orbit and its deletion-stack labels, followed by exact stress testing using integer square root and no floating-point decisions.

claims.claim: Under the zero-no-op-round convention, the exact worst-case values for n=1,...,9 are 0,1,3,6,9,12,18,21,26.
claims.evidence: Complete enumeration covered sum_{n=1}^9 n!=409,113 permutations. Each trajectory used exact tuple operations, was checked against the literal marking implementation, and was cross-checked by the independent phase formulation. The computed maxima were exactly [0,1,3,6,9,12,18,21,26], supplying both exhaustive upper bounds and attaining lower bounds.
claims.witness: For n=1 use (1); for 2<=n<=8, (n,1,...,n-1) attains the stated value; for n=9, (3,9,4,5,1,2,6,7,8) takes 26 rounds.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive lexicographic enumeration of every permutation for n=1,...,9 with cycle-checked exact simulation and an independent phase-count cross-check.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for an asymptotically tight worst-case classification. The draft rigorously establishes W(n)=O(n^2), thereby resolving the highlighted omega(n^2) subquestion negatively, but its proved lower bound remains only Omega(n). It therefore leaves an asymptotic gap and does not fully determine W(n). The final writeup explicitly acknowledges that gap and claims only partial resolution, so claimed_resolution=PARTIAL is accurate and not overclaimed.
